title: Wet filter paper can split black ink into the colours it’s made of
body: Put a dot of ink on filter paper and dip the edge in a solvent. The solvent creeps up the paper by capillary action and carries the ink with it, but each dye in the mix travels at its own speed: the more readily a dye dissolves in the solvent, the faster it moves, while dyes that cling to the paper fall behind. The mixture comes apart into bands, and a sample that shows more than one colour must contain more than one kind of molecule.

slides.alt: Animation of a strip of white filter paper with a black ink dot, dipped in a beaker of solvent. As the wet front climbs, the dot splits into yellow, magenta and blue bands. A close-up diagram shows dye molecules sticking to paper fibres or moving with the solvent, then each band's Rf is measured.

slides.heading: One phase moves, one stays
slides.text: The solvent is the mobile phase: it flows up the paper. The stationary phase is the water trapped between the paper’s cellulose fibres. Each dye divides its time between the two, and that sets its speed.

slides.question: A dye moved 3 cm up the paper while the solvent front moved 12 cm. What is the dye’s Rf?
slides.explanation: Rf is the distance the dye travelled divided by the distance the solvent travelled: 3 ÷ 12 = 0.25. It always lies between 0 (stuck at the start) and 1 (moving with the solvent front).

slides.heading: Does this dye climb faster or lag behind?
slides.explanation: The more soluble a dye is in the solvent, the faster it migrates up the paper. A dye with Rf near 0 barely leaves the starting line.

events.text: Mikhail Tsvet develops it to separate plant pigments
He first uses the word chromatography in print
Martin and Synge win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry

slides.heading: A fitting name
slides.text: Tsvet’s surname is Russian for “colour”. He used the method on chlorophylls and carotenoids from plants. Today paper chromatography is mostly a teaching tool, and it works on colourless chemicals too, if a stain makes the spots visible afterwards.
